name: agy
summary: Antigravity CLI: non-interactive Gemini. Reads PDFs natively with OCR + per-page screenshots, so it can see figures that pdftotext cannot.
usage: agy --model gemini-4-argon-high --print='prompt text' (--model BEFORE --print, and use --print='...' with an equals sign or it eats the next flag as its prompt; 'agy models' lists gemini-4-argon-*, gemini-3.8-flash-*, also Claude and GPT-OSS models, which are not outside readers)
notes: Config in ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json: terminal sandbox on, deny ~/.ssh and ~/.gnupg; toolPermission proceed-in-sandbox; artifactReviewPolicy always-proceed; trusted workspace and recursive write_file allow for ~/Projects; dev-command allowlist (grok, jq, bun, python/pip/uv, bash, tee, ...); asks before rm -rf, git push --force, git reset --hard. No per-run read-only switch: verified 2026-10-27 that --mode plan still writes inside ~/Projects. As a reviewer, run it in a frozen copy outside ~/Projects (e.g. /tmp, chmod -R a-w): there headless write_file is auto-denied, but the whole turn then returns no output, so the prompt must still say not to write. Checksum before and after. NOT A REVIEW-LOOP READER for now (2026-10-29): from its terminal sandbox it reached the live office (office status returned the real store), so its recipe does not block office and review-loop step 3 rules it out, even in a stripped copy. It is the only reader that sees figures; fencing it (a deny for office in its settings) is untested.

name: claude
summary: Claude Code CLI headless (claude -p): the Claude reader for review-loop, run like codex/grok from a reader's copy, never as a subagent
usage: cd <reader copy> && claude -p --model claude-opus-5-5 --no-session-persistence --allowedTools <named read-only commands, e.g. "Bash(ls:*)" "Bash(bun test:*)"> --disallowedTools "Edit" "Write" "NotebookEdit" "Bash(office:*)" -- 'brief' < /dev/null
notes: Verified 2026-10-29: started in a scratch folder it loads no project instructions and none of the author's memory (a subagent of the author's session does carry them, so never use one as a reader). With these flags it was refused office status, env office status, sh -c "office status", the full path to office, and a shell redirect, and had no file-writing tool; read-only tools (Read, Grep, Glob) need no flag. Never allow Bash wholesale. Report is stdout. Leaves an empty folder ~/.claude/projects/<copy path with / and . as -> even with --no-session-persistence: delete it with the copy.

name: codex
summary: Codex CLI 0.163. gpt-6-luna verified working. -s read-only enforces no-writes at the sandbox, which is why it is the best harness for an outside reviewer.
usage: codex exec -m gpt-6-luna -s read-only --skip-git-repo-check -C <dir> 'prompt' < /dev/null   (-s read-only|workspace-write|danger-full-access; -i <png> to attach screenshots; from a background shell add < /dev/null or it waits on stdin forever and prints nothing)
notes: Verified 2026-10-27: -s read-only blocks writes ('Read-only file system') and still runs shell reads. Since /etc/apparmor.d/bwrap was added that day it uses real bubblewrap (no more userns warning), which gives the sandbox a fresh /dev: folders under /dev/shm are invisible to it, so do not put a reviewer's copy there. As a review-loop reader (2026-10-29): from -s read-only it cannot reach the office ('daemon not running'), so it may read the office's own repository. It prints its whole transcript to stdout; the report is the text after the last line that reads exactly 'codex' (cut at 'tokens used'). Run it from the reader's copy (-C <copy>).

name: grok
summary: Grok CLI on Frank's paid grok.com account; headless reviewer held to read-only by its sandbox
usage: grok -m grok-4.7 -p 'prompt'   (headless single-turn; 'grok models' lists grok-4.7 default, -4.7-build-fast, -4.6, -4.5; logged in via grok.com). As a reviewer that may run code but not write: --sandbox read-only --always-approve --no-subagents --disable-web-search < /dev/null. Without shell: --permission-mode dontAsk --tools read_file,list_dir,grep
notes: Verified 2026-10-27: --sandbox read-only blocks writes at the OS level ('Permission denied') once /etc/apparmor.d/bwrap lets bwrap make user namespaces (added that day). The read-only profile still allows writes to /tmp, /var/tmp and ~/.grok, so keep a reviewer's frozen copy out of /tmp. --permission-mode plan alone is useless headless: it refuses even a find and returns nothing. As a review-loop reader (2026-10-29): from --sandbox read-only it cannot reach the office ('daemon not running'), so it may read the office's own repository; the no-shell mode (--tools read_file,list_dir,grep) cannot run office at all.

name: opencode
summary: OpenCode CLI, used only for its free models (DeepSeek, GLM, ...)
usage: opencode run --model opencode/<free-model> --file a.json 'prompt'  (opencode models | grep free; --file caps at 10MiB; --format json). As a reviewer: OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT='{"permission":{"edit":"deny","bash":"deny","webfetch":"deny"}}' in front
notes: Free models only, never a paid one (Frank). Verified 2026-10-27: --agent plan is NOT read-only headless; it ran 'touch WROTE.txt' through bash and succeeded. The deny config is untested live because the free usage limit was hit on every free model that day (deepseek-v4.1-flash-free, glm-5.3-flash-free, mimo-v2.6-flash-free; nemotron-3-ultra-free 'unavailable'). As a review-loop reader: with the bash deny config it cannot run office at all (config-enforced; untested live, see above).

name: reader-copy
summary: How to make a review-loop reader's copy that leaves out the office's files (review-loop step 3)
usage: rsync -a --exclude=AGENTS.md --exclude=CLAUDE.md --exclude=.claude --exclude=.agents --exclude=/review-loop --exclude=node_modules --exclude=.venv <repo>/ <copy>/   then link node_modules/.venv back in if readers run code
notes: Unanchored excludes drop AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md/.claude/.agents at every level; /review-loop is anchored (unanchored it also drops skills/review-loop). Keep any of them when they are part of the work. Copy, clone or export: never a git worktree of the live repo, which the office counts as the same project. Put copies under ~/.cache (not /tmp or /var/tmp: grok may write there; not /dev/shm: codex cannot see it). Checked 2026-10-29: no global instruction file (~/.codex/AGENTS.md, ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, ~/.gemini/GEMINI.md, ~/AGENTS.md) mentions the office; re-check if a reader starts checking in again.
